sources.citation: Gilmore, Perry. 1979. A Children's Pidgin: The Case of a Spontaneous Pidgin for Two. Sociolinguistic Working Paper No. 64. Austin, TX: Southwest Educational Development Laboratory. ERIC ED250935.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only phonological content is a list of segmental adaptation rules for Swahili and English loans (voiceless > voiced stops, dental fricative > bilabial/alveolar stop, syllable additions/reductions e.g. cowboy > kalabox) and a footnoted pronunciation guide giving vowel values; no mention of word stress, accent or tone. 'Intonation' and 'rhythm, meter' occur only in transcript stage directions and a remark on verbal play with repeated moja.
